prov.whatTheProductSHIPS: one prov anchor whose children in DOM order are: b granted figure, sep, b demonstrated figure, sep, span pack key, span granted counting rule, sep, span demonstrated counting rule. The prov class is display inline-flex with gap 6px, so DOM order is paint order and the two figures sit together at the head with their two rules together at the tail. Source: web/index.html line 314 and its G-93 comment at line 308, resolved by web/app.js applyIdentity from packSources() in src/city-identity.mjs.
prov.proposedAPI: a discriminated union on the props. Arm one is today's component unchanged: source required, detail optional. Arm two adds secondClaim with a source and a detail where BOTH are required, and makes the top-level detail REQUIRED. Render order follows the product exactly: source, sep, secondClaim source, sep, detail, sep, secondClaim detail.
whatItREFUSES: a second figure with no counting rule of its own, because the second claim detail is not optional
a second figure while the first figure has no counting rule, because the union makes detail required on the two-claim arm

a third claim, because there is no shape for one and the product ships none. A claims array would have made N representable and N has no product counterpart, so a case built on it could never fail for the right reason
reordering the interleave, because the order is emitted by the component and is not a prop
prov.theTrapThisAPIcarries: the second claim source renders next to source and the second claim detail renders at the far end, so the reading order of the props is not the reading order of the output. That is the PRODUCT shape and a wrapper must follow it rather than tidy it. Held three ways rather than by a doc comment: a law test asserting the exact rendered child order, a markup-parity case against the shipped nav-foot chip, and a prove:gates injection.
prov.whyNOTaclaimsArray: the shipped chip groups figures at the head and rules at the tail. An array of figure-and-rule pairs reads as figure, rule, figure, rule and would either render markup the product does not have or need a silent reordering step inside the component. src/status.tsx already states the governing rule in its own words: wrapping would make the component render markup the product does not have, which is the one thing a wrapper must never do.
